overview: White plays 3.Bd2, which leaves the d4 pawn only defended by the queen behind the bishop. Black can take 3...Bxd4 and give White time, while White aims for development. I am unsure of the exact follow-up and treat it as a rare trick line.

white_ideas.idea: Develop with Nc3 and Nf3 for the pawn
Open the position with c3 and Bc3-type ideas

black_ideas.idea: Take d4 with the bishop and hold it

typical_structures.structure: White bishop on d2 in the way

character.notes: Unclear but White pays a pawn for little.

gambit.notes: Black can take d4 and keep it.

soundness.notes: White seems to have little for the pawn.

character.reason: A pawn-down tricky line with forcing tries for White.

gambit.reason: The d4 pawn is given and Black can keep it.

soundness.reason: White gets little for the pawn.

structure.reason: The d-pawn goes and the d-file is partly open.

level.reason: A dubious line is not Beginner.

plans.reason: The pawn is meant to be repaid with time.
